NONE: › a large, pale green bean that can be eaten
› a very poor and crowded area of a city in Brazil

U: B2 [ U ] the support or approval of something or someone
› to support or approve of something
C1 When something is in your favour, it gives you an advantage.
對…有利，使…處於有利的位置
› If a judge finds in someone's favour, he or she says that that person is not guilty.

C: B1 [ C ] a kind action that you do for someone
C usually plural: › [ C usually plural ] an advantage that you give to someone, such as money or a good job, especially when this is unfair
› [ C usually plural ] a small present that you give to every guest at a wedding, party, etc.
（在婚禮、聚會等上發給客人的）小禮物

NONE: › to support or prefer one particular possibility
› to give an advantage to someone or something, in an unfair way

example: These plans are unlikely to find favour unless the cost is reduced.
這些計劃除非縮減費用，否則不大可能得到支持。
The Council voted in favour of a £200 million housing development.
政務委員會投票贊成耗資兩億英鎊的新建住宅區計劃。
She is out of favour (= unpopular) with her colleagues.
她在同事當中人緣不好。
Her economic theories are in favour (= popular) with the current government.
她的經濟理論獲得現任政府的贊同。
He sent her presents in an attempt to win her favour.
他向她贈送禮物，企圖博得她的好感。
Are you in favour of a ban on smoking?
你贊同禁煙嗎？
I'm not in favour of hitting children.
我不贊同打孩子。
This candidate has a lot in her favour, especially her experience of teaching.
這位求職者有很多優勢，尤其是她執教的經驗。
She called to ask me a favour.
她打電話來請我幫個忙。
Could you do me a favour - would you feed my cat this weekend?
你能幫我個忙——這週末幫我餵貓嗎？
Several politicians were accused of dispensing favours to people who voted for them.
幾名政客被指責向投票支援他們的人提供好處。
wedding favours
婚禮贈客禮品
These are the running shoes favoured by marathon runners.
這些是馬拉松選手喜愛的跑鞋。
In the survey, a majority of people favoured higher taxes and better public services over (= rather than) tax cuts.
調查顯示，大多數人贊同提高賦稅並改善公共服務事業，不贊成削減賦稅。
[ + -ing verb ] I generally favour travelling by night, when the roads are quiet.
我一般喜歡夜裡趕路，那時候路上比較清靜。
A strong wind will favour the bigger boats.
強風對大船有利。
She always felt that her parents favoured her brother.
她總覺得父母偏愛弟弟。

NONE: › to be polite and kind enough to give something to someone

example: I've no idea what is happening - David has not favoured me with an explanation.
我不清楚是怎麼回事——大衛沒有給我任何解釋。

NONE: B2 showing that you like or approve of someone or something
B2 making you support or approve of someone or something
贏得贊許的；討人喜歡的
C2 giving you an advantage or more chance of success

example: We have had a favourable response to the plan so far.
到目前為止，關於此計劃我們得到的回饋是正面的。
She made a very favourable impression on us.
她給我們留下的印象非常好。
Note: opposite unfavourable

More examplesThe proposal has received a generally favourable reaction.Reactions to the proposal so far have been favourable.The new restaurant has received favourable reviews.Favourable market conditions helped him to make a big profit.The launch was assisted by favourable weather conditions.

NONE: A1 best liked or most enjoyed
最不喜歡的；特別不喜歡的
B1 a thing that someone likes best or enjoys most
最喜歡的東西；特別喜愛的東西
› a person who is treated with special kindness by someone in authority
C2 the person or animal most people expect to win a race or competition
最有希望獲勝的人（或動物）；比賽中最被看好的人（或動物）

example: my favourite restaurant/book/song
我最喜歡的餐館／書／歌曲
Cleaning the toilets is my least favourite job.
打掃廁所是我最不喜歡的工作。
How clever of you to buy chocolate chip cookies - they're my favourites.
你真聰明，買了帶巧克力顆粒的餅乾——這是我的最愛。
the teacher's favourite
老師的寵兒
Great Gold is the favourite in the 2.00 race at Epsom.
巨金被認為最有希望在埃普索姆賽馬會中獲得兩英里賽的冠軍。
[ + to infinitive ] Brazil are favourites to win this year's World Cup.
巴西隊是今年世界盃賽的奪冠熱門。

NONE: › a famous person, especially a politician, who is supported and praised by people in the area they come from
故鄉的驕子（尤指政治家）
› unfair support shown to one person or group, especially by someone in authority
（尤指當權者不公平的）偏愛，偏袒

example: A parent must be careful not to show favouritism towards any one of their children.
家長必須注意不要偏愛任何一個子女。
